Episodes 1 to 7 of 18 are authored: 381 entities, 2,682 exact mentions in original-en and 2,695 in modern-en, 380 of the 381 bound in the older edition and 378 in the modern one, 65 focused tests passing, content revision 2026-09-15.7. NEXT: episode 8 (Lestrygonians, 385 paragraphs), Bloom's lunch. 5,207 paragraphs remain; the long ones are 15 (Circe, 1,441), 17 (Ithaca, 654), 11 (Sirens, 635), 12 (566) and 10 (546); episode 18 (Penelope) is eight paragraphs of monologue and will be the densest in the book.

THE RULE THAT GOVERNS THIS BOOK: A SURNAME IS ALMOST NEVER ONE MAN, SO KEY BY DEFAULT AND ALIAS ONLY ON PROOF. There is no 'Bloom' default and 4:38 -- SLIEVE BLOOM, the mountains in Offaly -- is deliberately not keyed. THE SURNAME DEDALUS CHANGES HANDS AT EPISODE 6: episodes 1-2 key it to STEPHEN, episode 6 to his father SIMON. EPISODE 7 HAS BOTH MEN IN IT -- 7:21 and 7:109-7:168 are Simon, 7:258 and 7:497 are his son, who comes in after his father goes out. A test pins the exceptions. Other sharp cases so far: TWO O'CONNELLS in one paragraph (6:330, keyed by occurrence, caught by the adjacency sweep); LEOPOLD is Bloom at 5:67 and THE DUKE OF ALBANY at 5:121; PETER is three men in six paragraphs (5:95, 5:100, 5:107); BUSHE is three men in two paragraphs (7:382, where the editor corrects himself out of Kendal Bushe); TWO PENELOPES one line apart at 7:519-7:520 (Homer's, then Penelope Rich); TWEEDY is three people; FRIDAY at 6:337 is Crusoe's man and then the weekday.

THE MODERN EDITION IS A REWRITE AND CHANGES THE CAST OF A PARAGRAPH IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. It DELETES names (Chrysostomos 1:9, Mercury 1:293, Loyola 1:101, Adam Findlater and Dan Tallon 4:37, Hanlon 4:13, Wren 6:204, the Joe Miller 7:293) and SUPPLIES names Joyce did not write (Aristotle 3:0, Brian Boru 3:57, Deasy 3:10, Queen Victoria 3:94, M'Coy 5:27, Daniel O'Connell 6:106/6:277/6:278, Madame Bloom 6:104, Shakespeare 6:333, Martha 6:386, Nannetti 7:42 and 7:62, Bloom 7:67, Patrick Dignam 7:99, Gallaher 7:358, Mario 7:27, Long John Fanning 7:45). IT ALSO SPLITS JOYCE'S COMPOUNDS, which makes a name bindable that was not: 'Jesusmario' (7:27) becomes 'Jesus-Mario', as 'pseudomalachi' (9:194) becomes 'false Malachi' and 'Sonmulligan' (9:331) 'Son-Mulligan'. Two entities are reachable in one edition only: BRIAN BORU in the modern alone, ADAM FINDLATER in the older alone.

A SILENT BINDER LIMITATION THAT APPLIES TO EVERY BOOK IN THIS LIBRARY: reviewed_aliases.py guards alias matches with \w, AND AN UNDERSCORE SATISFIES \w, so an alias whose occurrence sits inside Gutenberg italics (_like this_) BINDS NOTHING AND NOTHING REPORTS IT. Three cases, all keyed now: '_Los Demiurgos_' 3:1, '_Matcham's Masterstroke_' 4:162, '_That's not Mulcahy_' 6:325. Two of the three were found by the EDITION-ASYMMETRY CENSUS, because the modern edition has no italics -- run that census on every episode; it is the most productive single check in this book after the occurrence list. Over all 18 episodes the italic check still reports STEPHEN at 15:1133 (a stage direction) and PATRICE at 16:212, which is NOT Patrice Egan but 'the faubourg Saint Patrice'.

DELIBERATELY UNBOUND IN EPISODE 7 AND RECORDED: 'His grace' at 7:30 and 'the archbishop's letter' at 7:86 are almost certainly William J. Walsh, cast in episode 5, but this episode never says so and the inference is left to the reader. Newspapers and columns are not cast (Uncle Toby's page, Paddy Kelly's Budget, Pue's Occurrences, the Skibbereen Eagle, the Old Woman of Prince's street), nor 'the Joe Miller' at 7:293, which is a joke-book used as a common noun -- the modern edition writes 'the joke', which settles it.
